Internship / Graduates Opportunity

This internship is designed for university students and recent graduates who want to develop practical business analysis skills and gain valuable workplace experience before entering the professional job market.

You will work alongside business management and gain exposure to actual business activities, operational reporting, financial analysis, sales performance and business development.

Educations must be in : Masters In commerce , Business analytics , or Finance

Key Responsibilities

* Collect, organise and analyse business data.
* Prepare Excel reports, dashboards and management reports.
* Analyse sales, quotations, orders and production performance.
* Monitor project costs, expenses and business performance.
* Identify opportunities to improve business processes.
* Assist with developing KPIs and performance tracking systems.
* Conduct market and competitor research.
* Support business planning and strategic decision-making.
* Prepare presentations and recommendations for management.
* Assist in implementing business improvement projects.

Practical Industry Experience You Will Gain

During your internship, you will have the opportunity to work on real business projects, including:

* **Business Performance Analysis:** Understand how an engineering business operates and measure its performance.
* **Financial Analysis:** Learn about job costing, revenue, expenses and profitability.
* **Operations Management:** Analyse manufacturing activities, production time and resource utilisation.
* **Sales & Marketing Analysis:** Review quotations, customer enquiries and sales opportunities.
* **Business Intelligence:** Develop Excel dashboards, reports and KPI tracking systems.
* **Process Improvement:** Identify administrative inefficiencies and recommend practical solutions.
* **Strategic Planning:** Participate in business growth planning and management reporting.

What You Will Gain

* Practical experience working in a real Australian manufacturing business.
* Exposure to real business data and management decisions.
* Hands-on experience with Microsoft Excel, reporting and data analysis.
* Understanding of business operations and manufacturing processes.
* Development of analytical, communication and problem-solving skills.
* Experience working with management and different business functions.
* Professional workplace exposure to strengthen your future CV.
* Opportunity to build industry connections and professional references, subject to performance and company policy.

Who Should Apply?

* University students studying Business Analytics, Business Administration, Commerce, Management, Accounting or related degrees.
* Students looking for practical industry experience.
* Recent graduates wanting to develop workplace skills.
* Candidates with an interest in business operations, data analysis and continuous improvement.

Skills Required

* Basic to intermediate Microsoft Excel skills.
* Good analytical and problem-solving abilities.
* Strong written and verbal communication.
* Willingness to learn and take responsibility.
* Positive attitude and attention to detail.
* Knowledge of Power BI, accounting software or data analytics is an advantage but not essential.

Why Join Us?

At Aadarsh Engineering, you will not just observe business activities. You will participate in real projects, work with actual business information and understand how management decisions are made in an operating engineering business.

**Build your practical experience today and prepare yourself for tomorrow's career.**

How to Apply

Interested candidates are invited to submit their CV along with a brief introduction explaining their interest in this internship.

**About Syenta**  
Syenta is pioneering a new era in semiconductor manufacturing with our groundbreaking Localized Electrochemical Manufacturing (LEM) technology. Our manufacturing products build cutting edge advanced packaging for the semiconductor industry by combining patterning and metallization into a single tool. We do that by achieving high-speed, high-resolution metallization at significantly lower costs and energy use, while minimizing emissions and waste.

Founded in Australia, our growing footprint in the US represents a key milestone in our journey. We are building a world-class team where seasoned engineers and ambitious emerging talent collaborate to solve some of the toughest challenges in semiconductor manufacturing.

**About the Role**

We are seeking a **Process Engineer** **Intern** to join Syenta’s Sydney process team **immediately**. This will be a **6-month full-time internship**. You’ll be working directly on the processes at the heart of Syenta’s technology - running experiments, developing your technical understanding, and contributing ideas that genuinely shape how we work.

From day one you’ll have real deliberate mentorship from senior experts who are invested in your development. We’re looking for someone who is hungry to learn, takes ownership of their work, and wants to make an impact at a company redefining how semiconductors are made.

**Responsibilities**

*Process & Experimentation*

* Following existing standard operating procedures (SOPs) to support Syenta’s stamp fabrication process and stamp pre-plating process through hands-on laboratory work, experimental runs, and active participation in team discussions.
* Execute parameter sweeps, design of experiments (DOE) runs, and repeatability tests, growing into increasing ownership of experimental design over time.
* Prepare substrates, consumables, and materials; operate prototype equipment with guidance; and perform routine maintenance and troubleshooting.

*Data & Analysis*

* Maintain clear and accurate records of all laboratory work to ensure reproducibility and knowledge sharing across the team.
* Assist with data analysis, plotting, and summary reporting.
* Identify anomalies and unexpected results and work collaboratively with the team to investigate and understand them.

*Communication & Collaboration*

* Work alongside the broader team to achieve technical milestones and resolve issues as they arise.
* Share progress updates with the LEM team and actively contribute to group discussions on results and next steps.
* Support preparation and delivery of demonstrations of Syenta’s LEM technology to visitors, partners, and investors.

*Ownership & Impact*

* Take ownership of assigned projects and deliverables, seeing them through to completion.
* Proactively identify improvements to performance or workflows and speak up about them.

**Requirements**

* Existing access to SNF (previously known as RPF at the University of Sydney) and/or UNSW-ANFF.
* Hands-on and/or knowledge of experience in microfabrication processes and tools.
* Strong attention to detail, with a methodical approach to laboratory work and a commitment to maintaining clear and accurate records.
* A fast learner who goes deep – building real understanding, not just surface familiarity.
* Analytical problem solver when the path forward isn’t obvious – breaking problems down and making progress rather than waiting for clarity to arrive.
* Confident enough to contribute ideas around senior team members and grounded enough to learn from them.
* A genuine interest in growing with a fast-paced, innovative company and contributing to the development of transformative technology.

This role would be well suited to students currently studying in Nanotechnology, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, or related field.

**Bonus points for:**

* Exposure to semiconductor, MEMS, electrochemistry, PCB, or advanced materials processes.
* Familiarity with metrology tools such as optical microscopy, FIB-SEM, SEM, AFM, or conductivity measurements.

**Why Choose Syenta?**

We’re passionate about building a diverse, people-first company. Our culture of collaboration and mutual respect fuels innovation capable of redefining an industry. At Syenta, you’ll have the opportunity to take ownership, lead high-impact teams, and shape the future of semiconductor manufacturing.

**What We Offer**

* Competitive salary
* Early-stage equity opportunities
* 12% superannuation contributions
* Flexible leave policies and a strong work-life balance
* Professional growth in a high-impact, fast-growing deep-tech startup
* Team events and collaborative culture, including company-wide gatherings in Australia

**About Anthropic**
-------------------

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About Beneficial Deployments**
--------------------------------

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.

**About the Role**
------------------

We're looking for an Applied AI Architect to join Beneficial Deployments, focused on helping nonprofits and research institutes in APAC get real value from Claude. You'll be the technical lead for a portfolio of partners, working alongside our Account Executives from first conversation through deployment, and you'll support a wider set of accounts through learning sessions. With nonprofits, you'll find where Claude makes a real difference to their mission and their operations. With research institutes, you'll help researchers and the teams who support them use Claude in work they can check and stand behind. You'll design solutions that fit each partner's budget, data and teams, and turn early pilots into lasting adoption. What works for one partner becomes something others across the region and beyond can use.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Serve as the primary technical advisor to a portfolio of nonprofits and research institutes from discovery through deployment, turning their priorities into scoped use cases with clear measures of success.
* Partner with Account Executives on account plans, discovery and technical evaluation.
* Design and demo solutions with Claude, the API and Claude Code and Science for nonprofits and research institutes
* Help researchers evaluate Claude on their own questions and data before they rely on it, and be plain about its limits.
* Guide partners through security review, data governance and procurement, including rules that differ by country and limits on how research data can be used.
* Support a wider portfolio of accounts through learning sessions and enablement.
* Run workshops and trainings that build AI fluency across partner teams, from program staff to research groups.
* Build reusable assets (reference designs, connectors, prompt and eval templates) so one partner's work helps the next.
* Spot patterns across partners, bring field insight back to Product and Research, and help partners measure what changed.
* Travel up to 30% to partner sites for workshops, technical deep dives and relationship building.

**You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have**
---------------------------------------

* 7-10 years in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, sales engineering, forward-deployed engineering or technical consulting.
* A track record of getting lean, skeptical or slow-moving teams with many stakeholders to adopt technology and keep using it, including working through how they buy and govern it.
* Hands-on experience building with LLM APIs: you have built and evaluated working prototypes or agents, and can guide a partner's own engineers on architecture and evals. You don't need to write production code.
* The ability to earn the trust of researchers and other specialists: you can show how you tested something, where it fails and what you don't know yet.
* Clear written and spoken communication across a broad audience. The ability to explain technical tradeoffs to program leads, researchers, operations staff and executives.
* Patience with long buying and partnership cycles, a knack for knowing how to make them go smoothly, and real care for public benefit.
* A track record of agency and autonomy: you spot what needs doing before anyone asks, agree that it matters, drive it to a finished result and know when to pull others in.
* Comfort operating in ambiguity: you bring clarity to fuzzy problems, wear multiple hats and do whatever it takes to further the mission.
* Bonus if you've worked with or at nonprofits, foundations, research institutes or other mission-driven organizations, worked in a sales team, built multilingual products, or worked with partners in more than one country.

**About the Department**
------------------------

The Department of Industry, Science and Resources and our broader portfolio are integral to the Australian Government’s economic agenda. Our purpose is to help the government build a better future for all Australians through enabling a productive, resilient and sustainable economy, enriched by science and technology. We do this by:

* Growing innovative & competitive businesses, industries and regions
* Investing in science and technology
* Strengthening the resources sector.

The APS and the department offer a clear direction and meaningful work. You will be able to create positive impact in people’s lives whilst contributing to improved outcomes for Australia and our people.  
  
If you would like to feel a strong connection to your work and you are accountable, committed and open to change, join us in shaping Australia’s future.  
  
Please see the APSC’s APS Employee Value Proposition for more information on the benefits and value of employment within the APS.  

**About the team**
------------------

The Temperature and Humidity Team maintains and disseminates Australia’s primary standards for temperature, humidity and trace moisture measurement. We deliver high-accuracy calibration and measurement services to Australian industry, government and research organisations in sectors including advanced manufacturing, semiconductor processing, pharmaceuticals, defence and aerospace, clean energy including hydrogen. The team operates specialised humidity generation and measurement facilities covering relative humidity, dew-point and frost-point temperature, and trace moisture in gases. We work within an ISO/IEC 17025-accredited quality system and undertake research and capability development to improve Australia’s national measurement infrastructure.

**The opportunity**
-------------------

Start or build your scientific or engineering career at Australia’s national measurement authority. With structured training and support from experienced scientists and engineers, you will develop specialist capability in precision temperature and humidity measurement while contributing to nationally significant calibration services and Australia’s primary measurement standards.

**What’s in it for you?**
-------------------------

Join a community of professionals committed to technical measurement excellence and cutting-edge research. We invest in advanced facilities, foster collaboration with leading institutions and support innovation. You will work with people who have diverse skill sets including scientists, engineers, policy specialists and regulatory professionals.  
  
This role provides an excellent opportunity to develop specialist expertise in humidity metrology while working with advanced humidity generation and high-accuracy reference measurement systems. You will build strong capabilities in measurement uncertainty, metrological traceability and laboratory quality systems within an ISO/IEC 17025-accredited environment, while contributing to the design, automation, validation and commissioning of new national measurement capabilities. Working alongside experienced scientists, engineers and metrologists, you will apply your technical skills to solve real-world measurement challenges for Australian industry and research organisations, participate in applied research projects, and progress towards becoming an authorised signatory and recognised technical specialist in humidity measurement.  
  
As part of the Department of Industry, Science and Resources, employees at NMI are covered by an enterprise agreement and benefits include:

* Parental leave.
* A vacation care subsidy.
* $235 annual healthy lifestyle subsidy.
* Access to study assistance.
* Access to Employee Assistance Program - health, wellbeing, counselling and support when needed.

**Our ideal candidate**
-----------------------

We are seeking an early career scientist or engineer keen to apply their skills to generate practical impact for Australian community.  
  
Our ideal candidate will:

* Hold a tertiary qualification in physics, chemistry, engineering or a related discipline.
* Demonstrate ability to apply your scientific and analytical expertise to solve practical problems.
* Have a curious mindset and ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills.
* Have experience with identifying and resolving problems with equipment and instrumentation.
* Demonstrate sound judgement, initiative and a commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes.
* Be organised, adaptable and able to manage competing priorities.
* Communicate effectively and work collaboratively with colleagues, clients and stakeholders.

We are looking for individuals who bring personal integrity and a sense of purpose, and who embody NMI's values of being Inclusive, Innovative, Accountable, Adaptable, Influential and Strategic.  
  
Our department has a commitment to inclusion and diversity, with an ambition of being the best possible place to work. This reflects the importance we place on our people and on creating a workplace culture where each and every one of us is valued and respected for our contribution. Our ideal candidate adds to this culture and our workplace in their own way.

**What you will do**
--------------------

Following structured training and working under the guidance of experienced measurement scientists, you will progressively develop the technical competence, judgement and independence required to become a recognised specialist in humidity measurement. You will:

* Take responsibility for planning, managing and delivering accurate, high-quality calibration and measurement services within agreed timeframes.
* Maintain and improve the laboratory quality system, including validation, verification and quality assurance activities.
* Support research by working with experienced scientists to develop and validate new primary measurement standards, for example trace moisture standards for the semiconductor and hydrogen economy.
* Use engineering, software and data analysis skills to enhance automation of complex bespoke measurement apparatus.
* Investigate technical issues, analyse measurement results and assist with troubleshooting laboratory equipment and systems.
* Build productive working relationships and communicate effectively with clients, colleagues, technical experts and other stakeholders regarding technical requirements, work progress, results and emerging issues.
* Contribute to a safe, respectful and collaborative team environment and support the effective operation of the laboratory.

**Eligibility**
---------------

To be eligible for employment in the APS and the department, candidates must be Australian Citizens.  
  
Positions require a Baseline security clearance and successful candidates will be required to obtain and maintain a clearance at this level.

**Notes**
---------

This is a Sydney-based laboratory role. Flexible work arrangements may be considered where they are compatible with operational and laboratory requirements. Please contact the contact officer to discuss this further.

A merit pool may be established and used to fill future vacancies within 18 months from the date the vacancy was first advertised in the Gazette.

**Application information**
---------------------------

Your application must not contain any classified or sensitive information. This includes in your application responses, CV and any other documents. The selection panel may not consider applications containing classified information.  
  
Please provide a pitch explaining how your skills, knowledge and experience will be relevant to this role and why you are the best candidate for the position. Your pitch can contain no more than 500 words and should align to the key duties listed above.  
  
You may use AI tools to support your application. However, all content must be accurate, authentic, and reflect your own capability in line with APS merit principles. For further guidance, please refer to the APSC’s Principles for candidate use of AI in recruitment.  
  
Please complete your application online and provide your current CV with your application. (CVs must be in .doc, .docx, or .pdf format).  
  
Accessible application documentation is available in other formats on request. Please contact recruitment@industry.gov.au or (02) 6276 1235 if you require assistance with your application.  
  
Please refer to our Applying for a position information for additional information on how to apply.

**Contact Information**
-----------------------

For more information regarding this opportunity, please contact Wenwen Lei on 02 8467 3436 or via email on wenwen.lei@measurement.gov.au

**YOUR IMPACT**

We are seeking a commercial, relationship-driven professional to join our APAC Corporate Access franchise as a Vice President, with responsibility for covering Australia and New Zealand (ANZ). In this role, you will be the primary point of contact for ANZ corporates, building deep, trusted relationships with their C-suite executives and Investor Relations (IR) teams, and connecting them with our local and global institutional investor base.

  

While end-to-end execution excellence is fundamental, origination capability is critical to this role. You will proactively identify market themes, originate differentiated access opportunities, build relationships with C-suite executives and Investor Relations (IR) leaders, and drive commercial monetization across the Goldman Sachs markets franchise.

  

**OUR IMPACT**

Our core value is building strong relationships with our institutional clients, which include corporations, financial service providers, and fund managers. We help them buy and sell financial products on exchanges around the world, raise funding, and manage risk. This is a dynamic, entrepreneurial team with a passion for the markets, with individuals who thrive in fast-paced, changing environments and are energized by a bustling trading floor.

  

**TEAM DESCRIPTION**

Corporate Access originates and curates content for clients via close collaboration with our team members across Asia Pacific. Our core clients are institutional investors including long-only asset managers, hedge funds, sovereign wealth funds and pension plans. We also identify, prospect and build relationships with corporate clients, including leading companies across Australia and New Zealand.

  

Content can be described as access to public and private corporates, industry experts, academics, government officials, Goldman Sachs thought leadership and subject matter experts. Corporate Access originates and executes thematic and regional events, including some of Goldman Sachs’ largest flagship conferences globally, regional field trips, post earning luncheons, non-deal roadshows, corporate days and reverse inquiries. The team works closely with Sales, Research, Banking, Equity Capital Markets, Private Wealth and the Executive Office to deliver best-in-class content and speakers that match clients’ needs.

  

Corporate Access is currently seeking a highly-motivated and experienced candidate to join our Syndey office as a Vice President covering ANZ. The successful candidate will own the ANZ corporate relationship network and be a key originator of ANZ-related access opportunities for our global client base.

  

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Build and maintain strong, long-term relationships with ANZ corporates, including C-suite executives, CFOs and IR leaders, as their trusted partner for investor engagement in APAC and globally
* Proactively originate corporate access mandates with ANZ corporates, identifying compelling company, macro and sector themes that resonate with institutional investors
* Expand the ANZ corporate universe by prospecting new relationships across listed and private companies, and convert them into post result events, roadshows, corporate days, field trips and conference participation
* Drive and own the bespoke corporate access process with key institutional clients, matching ANZ corporate content to investor interests
* Work closely with Research, Banking, Equity Capital Markets and Sales teams in Australia, New Zealand and across Asia to leverage Goldman Sachs’ franchise and deepen corporate relationships
* Understand client needs and anticipate ways to enhance the client service experience in close collaboration with Sales teams
* Lead the end-to-end planning and execution of ANZ-related events, including agenda creation, client targeting, logistics and post-event follow-up
* Support thematic events and flagship conferences by sourcing and securing ANZ corporate speakers and participants
* Handle a high volume of requests supporting external clients as well as communication with internal stakeholders
* Drive business analytics with the team to produce regular reporting on client and corporate activity.
  

**SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE WE ARE LOOKING FOR**

* Prefer 5+ years of relevant experience in corporate access, equity sales, investor relations, equity research or investment banking, with a proven track record of originating business
* Established relationships with ANZ corporates, including C-suite executives and IR leaders, and the credibility to open doors and secure access
* Strong knowledge of the ANZ market, including key sectors, listed companies and the themes that matter to global investors
* Demonstrated ability to originate, with a commercial mindset and the initiative to turn relationships into differentiated access opportunities and measurable revenue impact
* Excellent relationship-building, influencing and communication skills, with the presence to engage confidently with senior executives and institutional investors
* Relevant Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification with an excellent academic record
* Proven ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment while managing multiple competing priorities
* Strong attention to detail and strong organizational skills
* High degree of integrity and solid work ethic
* Entrepreneurial, proactive and self-motivated

Overview:

**170+ Years Strong. Industry Leader. Global Impact.**  
At Pinkerton, the mission is to protect our clients. To do this, we provide enterprise risk management services and programs specifically designed for each client. The Senior Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) Specialist - ANZ, assigned to one of Pinkerton’s largest global clients, will act as the Deputy to the EHS Manager, supporting multi-site EHS operations, compliance, and risk management across Australia and New Zealand. This role provides senior-level support on incident management, psychosocial risk management, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement, and deputizes for the EHS Manager on operational and stakeholder matters when required.

Responsibilities:

* Represent Pinkerton's core values of integrity, vigilance, and excellence.

  Deputize for the EHS Manager in their absence, including representing EHS at leadership and regulator meetings.
* Support the rollout and continuous improvement of EHS management systems across all ANZ sites.
* Support the delivery of site-level training and awareness sessions, with an increased focus on psychosocial risk, emergency preparedness, and general safety topics.
* Assist in identifying, assessing, and managing psychosocial hazards, such as workload, bullying, harassment, and fatigue, in line with Work Health and Safety (WHS) and Health and Safety at Work Act (HSWA) requirements, and escalate higher-risk matters to the EHS Manager.
* Help coordinate worker consultation activities and feedback channels on health and safety matters, including psychosocial risk.
* Support serious incident investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive action tracking.
* Conduct hazard identification, risk assessments, and compliance audits across multiple sites.
* Prepare EHS performance reporting, key performance indicators (KPIs), and trend analysis for senior leadership.
* Monitor regulatory changes for WHS in Australia and the HSWA in New Zealand, and support compliance strategy updates.
* Support emergency preparedness planning and crisis response coordination across sites.
* Maintain relationships with regulators, Health and Safety Representative (HSR) and Health and Safety Committee (HSC) members, and external EHS partners.
* Mentor and support EHS Coordinators and Specialists across the region.
* Support environmental and sustainability compliance programs, including waste, emissions, and energy reporting.
* Assist with budget planning and resource allocation for EHS programs across ANZ.
* Present a professional image of the organization when speaking to regulators, stakeholders, and all levels of internal and external employees.
* All other duties, as assigned.

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in WHS, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related field, with eight to ten or more years of progressive EHS experience, including demonstrated multi-site or regional support and ownership, is required. A postgraduate qualification in WHS or Occupational Health and Safety (OHS), such as a Graduate Diploma or Master's degree, is preferred. Lead Auditor certification in ISO 45001 or ISO 14001 is preferred. Chartered membership or professional registration, such as the Australian Institute of Health and Safety (AIHS) or Certified Australian Health and Safety Professional (CAHSP), or equivalent, is preferred. Formal training or qualification in psychosocial risk management or workplace mental health is preferred. Prior experience operating in a deputy, acting-manager, or regional leadership capacity is preferred. Industry experience relevant to the organization's sector is preferred.

* Strong working knowledge of Australian WHS and New Zealand HSWA frameworks, including psychosocial hazard codes of practice.
* Able to support, design, and deliver EHS training programs, including psychosocial and emergency preparedness content.
* Able to support or lead incident investigations, root cause analysis, and regulatory liaison.
* Demonstrated mentoring and people leadership ability.
* Strong strategic, organizational, and analytical skills.
* Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
* Able to travel across ANZ, as needed.

**Working Conditions:**

With or without reasonable accommodation, requires the physical and mental capacity to effectively perform all essential functions;

* Exposure to sensitive and confidential information.
* Regular computer usage.
* Must be able to see, hear, speak, and write clearly in order to communicate with employees and stakeholders.
* Frequent sitting, standing, and/or walking.
* Travel across ANZ, as required.

**Who we are :** We are a health service that touches thousands of lives across the Northern Sydney Local Health District, together as a team of like-minded people. We are passionate, driven and have the skills and knowledge to care for our patients whilst creating the best services possible. Our teams have meaningful, interesting and rewarding work every day. We challenge and nurture each other, sharing our knowledge and experience so that we can deliver better care for everyone. There's a real sense of belonging here because we value and respect our patients, employees, and teams' voices. You'll feel a real privilege being a trusted caregiver in our patients, their families, their carers, and our communities' lives.

**About the Role**
  
Macquarie Hospital is a 195 bed facility comprised of 9 separate units, 8 of which are medium to long stay. The primary purpose of the position is for the clinical management and leadership of the Adult Rehabilitation stream which is comprised of Manning unit, Tarban unit, Bridgeview House and Cottages.
  
Manning unit assists consumers to gain insight into their mental illness and to maximise their level of functioning, thus improving quality of life. The unit provides a structured program for consumers requiring assistance with basic living skills with the aim of moving consumers, where possible, to a less restrictive environment. Consumers attend unit and Hospital Rehabilitation Programs for vocational/ pre-vocational, educational and leisure activities, and have access to the local community. A number of these consumers have been identified as in scope for the Pathways to Community Living Initiative (PCLI) programme and are working towards transition to community living.
  
Tarban unit population consists of consumers who are longer stay and treatment resistant. Consumers who also have a history of behavioral disturbance and require the level of security a locked unit provides them. The unit can also a provide short term admission to assist the consumer's recovery prior to being transferred to a less restrictive environment. It can function as an admission unit for the locked units.
  
Bridgeview House is the admission unit for the open, non-acute function of the hospital. The multidisciplinary team in partnership with consumers and their carers endeavour to promote better mental and physical health through the development of realistic consumer goals.
  
Cottages provides domestic style accommodation with varying levels of independent living. The team's aim is to empower consumers to achieve their optimal level of functioning within a least restrictive environment and to encourage and support social inclusion. Consumers attend rehabilitation and vocational programmes (where appropriate) both on and off the campus. There is an expectation that consumers who are living in independent cottages will be discharged into the community when suitable accommodation is available.

**Purpose of the Position**

The position will provide clinical management and treatment of consumers under your care in a Northern Sydney Local Health District (NSLHD) facility or service. This care will be provided within the scope of practice endorsed by the NSLHD Medical and Dental Appointments Advisory Committee (MDAAC).
  
Provision of clinical consultation services within NSLHD and contribution to the teaching and training of medical officers, students, graduates and other health care professionals and to research, evaluation and quality improvement activities.
  
Participation in the on-call roster as directed by the Clinical Director. Human Resources management. Financial management and consideration of the hospital budget when prescribing and ordering tests/treatments. Show capacity for warmth, empathy and sensitivity whilst interacting with consumers.

* MBBS or equivalent, currently registered or eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia. Applicants must have Fellowship of the Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists (FRANZCP) or be eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia as a Specialist Psychiatrist and/or overseas trained substantial specialist pathways. Applicants expecting to be awarded their FRANZCP within 3 months may be considered

* Consistently demonstrates behaviours that reinforce the CORE Values of our organisation; Collaboration, Openness, Respect and Empowerment. Demonstrates these behaviours with all stakeholders; colleagues, direct reports, as well as our patients and consumers, and those that care for them.

* Experience in treating serious mental illness and working within a team to promote rehabilitation and recovery with a strong interest and/or qualifications in adult mental health rehabilitation.

* Demonstrated capacity to provide effective clinical leadership within multidisciplinary teams.

* Communication skills of a high order, including those of negotiation, mediation and conflict resolution.

* Proven high performance as an experienced clinician and willingness to participate in an on-call roster and provide leadership and support to junior medical staff and participate in regular doctors' meetings.

* Sound knowledge of the Mental Health Act 2007 and Guardianship Act and their application with commitment to State, National and Local Mental Health policy.

* NSW Drivers Licence and the ability to drive.
